title: Emit structured upgrade logs + generate diagnostics tarball for Support/SRE triage
author: Jacob Stein
release_notes: Private installer now emits JSONL structured logs for upgrade execution (step-level timings, statuses, correlation/run ids).
Installer can generate a diagnostics tarball containing prechecks, plan, step timings, kubernetes events, and recent pod logs to speed up Support triage.
description:
Context: Upgrade/rollback work has surfaced a consistent issue during rehearsals and beta pilots: when an upgrade fails mid-run, operators and Support/SRE spend too long reconstructing what happened from unstructured logs and manual kubectl output. This PR adds (1) structured logging for the upgrade controller and (2) an auto-generated diagnostics bundle (tar.gz) that captures the key artifacts needed for rapid triage.

What this PR does: - Adds a structured event stream for upgrade execution in JSONL (one event per line) emitted to stdout and persisted to disk. - Introduces a diagnostics bundle generator that collects: precheck report JSON, upgrade plan JSON, step timing summary, raw step event stream, kubernetes events (namespaced), and recent pod logs for relevant Redwood namespaces/components. - Hooks bundle generation into upgrade failure paths (opt-in at first) and provides a manual CLI command for collection.

Structured upgrade logs: - New logger emits events with a stable schema: {"ts":"RFC3339Nano","level":"info|warn|error","run_id":"...","correlation_id":"...","command":"upgrade|rollback|precheck","phase":"precheck|backup|apply|validate|rollback","step_id":"...","step_name":"...","status":"started|succeeded|failed|skipped","duration_ms":1234,"component":"control-plane|gateway|runtime|observability","from_version":"...","to_version":"...","error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}. - Events are written to: ~/.redwood/private/runs/<run_id>/upgrade.events.jsonl and a human-readable summary remains on stderr/stdout for operator UX. - Correlation id is generated per run and propagated into every event (pairs with control plane correlation work landing in the monorepo).

Diagnostics bundle: - New command: redwood-private-installer diagnostics collect --run-id <id> --output <path> (defaults to ~/.redwood/private/diagnostics/redwood-private-diag-<run_id>.tar.gz). - New upgrade flag: --diagnostics-on-fail (default: true for non-interactive, false for interactive until UX signoff; see review notes). - Bundle includes: (1) metadata.json (installer version, git SHA, OS/arch, timestamp, run_id, correlation_id, target environment mode), (2) precheck.report.json (verbatim), (3) upgrade.plan.json, (4) steps.summary.json (derived timings + per-step outcome), (5) upgrade.events.jsonl, (6) kubernetes.events.txt (kubectl get events -A --sort-by=.lastTimestamp with filtering to relevant namespaces), (7) pod_describes/<ns>_<pod>.txt for pods matching labels app=redwood-* in redwood-system/redwood-observability namespaces, (8) pod_logs/<ns>_<pod>_<container>.log (tail N lines; default 500; configurable).

Security/safety: - Diagnostics collection explicitly excludes: kubeconfig files, raw Secret objects, and environment variables. - Implements a basic redaction pass over collected logs and describes to remove common secret patterns (Authorization: Bearer, x-api-key, aws_access_key_id, etc.) and emits a banner in metadata.json noting that redaction is best-effort and should be reviewed before sharing externally. - The bundle generator is careful to only shell out to kubectl when configured; on environments where kubectl is not available, the bundle still includes the installer artifacts and run logs.

Notes on operability: - Bundle creation should not fail the upgrade itself. If diagnostics collection fails, we emit a warning event diagnostics.bundle_failed and continue returning the original upgrade error code. - Collection uses a per-run temp dir and then creates a single tar.gz; temp dir is deleted on success unless --keep-temp is passed.

Testing: - Unit tests for event schema + JSONL writer (ensures every step emits started/succeeded/failed with duration). - Integration test (kind) verifying bundle contains expected files and that secrets are not collected. - Manual validation on staging VPC environment to confirm kubectl event capture is scoped and size-bounded.

Docs: - Updates CLI help for new diagnostics command and --diagnostics-on-fail flag. - Adds a short section in internal README for Support on where to find run_id and how to attach the tarball to Jira/Linear.

Follow-ups (not in scope): - Upload diagnostics bundles automatically to a customer-configured object store (requires more security review). - Add automatic linking of run_id to control plane audit log events (monorepo PR). - Expand redaction with a structured sanitizer and allow customer-supplied patterns.

Refs: ENG-2321; aligns with Private upgrade/rollback initiative supportability requirements.
commits: diagnostics: add bundle collector and tar.gz writer
upgrade: emit step lifecycle events to JSONL and include run_id/correlation_id
security: add best-effort log redaction + exclude secrets/kubeconfig
tests: add bundle contents test + structured logger schema tests
conversation:
Sean Gallagher (review): Love the direction. Two asks: (1) k8s events should be sorted and include namespaces; (2) cap pod log collection so we don't produce 2GB tarballs on noisy clusters. Also please emit an explicit metric/event for bundle generation success/failure so we can alert on collection regressions.

Jacob Stein (author): Added sort-by=.lastTimestamp and explicit filtering to redwood-* namespaces. Implemented caps: 500 lines default with --diagnostics-log-lines override. Added structured events diagnostics.bundle_started / diagnostics.bundle_succeeded / diagnostics.bundle_failed with duration_ms and output_path.

Allison Grant (review): Schema looks good, but please make sure every event includes run_id + correlation_id. Also, can we ensure error objects are stable (code + message) and avoid dumping raw stack traces into the JSONL?

Jacob Stein (author): Updated writer to enforce required fields; added tests that fail if run_id/correlation_id missing. Error object now uses {code,message} only; stack traces remain in human logs (stderr) but are not included in the JSONL events.

Marcus Lin (review): Security: please confirm we are not collecting secrets via `kubectl describe` output. It can include env var values depending on workload. Recommend: (1) do not collect `kubectl get secrets` or raw secret YAML; (2) add a redaction pass; (3) place a warning banner in bundle metadata.

Jacob Stein (author): Confirmed we do not fetch Secret objects. We do collect `kubectl describe pod` and pod logs, which can contain sensitive values; added best-effort redaction on collected outputs + metadata banner. Also added an option --diagnostics-skip-k8s to disable kubectl collection entirely.

Devon Price (review): CLI UX: --diagnostics-on-fail default behavior is important. I worry about interactive upgrades surprising operators with a bundle created and local disk usage. Suggest: default off in interactive mode and on in non-interactive/CI mode.

Jacob Stein (author): Implemented: if stdin is a TTY, default is false unless explicitly enabled. If non-interactive (or --yes), default is true. The help text now calls this out.

Rafael Mendes (review): Supportability: add installer version + config mode (vpc/onprem) + cluster endpoint (sanitized) to metadata.json, and include the raw precheck report even if upgrade didn't run.

Jacob Stein (author): Added installer version + git SHA + environment mode + cluster host (hostname only; no tokens) to metadata. Precheck report is included if present; if not present, bundle contains a note in metadata and continues.

CI bot: integration tests (kind) failed: TestDiagnosticsBundle_ContainsExpectedFiles expected kubernetes.events.txt but kubectl not installed in runner.

Jacob Stein (author): Updated integration test to run in a container image that includes kubectl, and added a second test path verifying graceful degradation when kubectl is absent.

Sean Gallagher (final): Approved. This should materially reduce time-to-triage. Please open a follow-up to wire the bundle path into incident-bot threads when we tag upgrade-related incidents.

Jacob Stein (author): Ack; will file follow-up and link to ENG-2321 rollout checklist.

Merge (squash) by Connor O'Brien: Merged into main.
